title: In silico analysis of the functional implications of drug resistance associated mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
authors: Pal, Ankita; Pal, Sapna; Mahapatra, Shweta; Pandey, Apratim; Mohanty, Debasisa
one_liner_zh: 该文结合WHO突变目录与可解释AI，分析结核分枝杆菌耐药突变在药物靶点3D结构中的位置及转录因子结合位点，涉及蛋白结构预测与稳定性评估，但核心是耐药机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移但深度不足。
abstract: The tuberculosis mutation catalogue published by World Health Organization (WHO) lists a large number of mutations based on the statistical significance of their association with resistance or susceptibility to various drugs. However, the mechanism by which they confer resistance to drugs is often not understood. To address these gaps, we combined known resistance associated mutations from the WHO catalogue and newly discovered mutations by explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). In order to decipher the mechanistic basis of drug resistance, we examined where these mutations occur in three dimensional (3D) structures of key drug targets, measured their proximity to drug binding sites and compared their abundance in drug resistant as well as drug susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb) strains. In parallel, we analyzed the functions of 112 newly identified drug resistance associated genes and compared them to known resistance genes, finding that most novel genes fall into different functional categories, though six share families with known resistance genes. We mapped coding mutations in all 112 novel genes to their functional domains, predicted 3D structures using Alphafold3 and evaluated their effects on protein stability. Notably, our study highlights that mutations in ribosomal proteins (RpsN1, RpsN2) and the transporter PstB may introduce new resistance mechanisms, such as altered drug interactions or increased drug efflux. Whereas, analysis of non coding mutations revealed that most are located at transcription factor binding sites, potentially affecting gene regulation. The current analysis provides valuable insights for the design of experiments to decode mechanistic basis of drug resistance tuberculosis.
abstract_zh: 世界卫生组织（WHO）发布的结核病突变目录基于突变与各种药物耐药性或敏感性关联的统计学显著性，列出了大量突变。然而，这些突变赋予耐药性的机制往往尚不清楚。为弥补这些空白，我们结合了WHO目录中已知的耐药相关突变以及通过可解释人工智能（XAI）新发现的突变。为了解析耐药性的机制基础，我们考察了这些突变在关键药物靶标三维（3D）结构中的位置，测量了它们与药物结合位点的接近程度，并比较了它们在耐药及药物敏感结核分枝杆菌（Mycobacterium tuberculosis, M.tb）菌株中的丰度。同时，我们分析了112个新鉴定的耐药相关基因的功能，并将其与已知耐药基因进行比较，发现大多数新基因属于不同功能类别，尽管有六个与已知耐药基因共享家族。我们将所有112个新基因中的编码突变映射到其功能域，使用Alphafold3预测三维结构，并评估了它们对蛋白质稳定性的影响。值得注意的是，我们的研究强调，核糖体蛋白（RpsN1、RpsN2）和转运蛋白PstB中的突变可能引入新的耐药机制，如改变药物相互作用或增加药物外排。而对非编码突变的分析显示，大多数位于转录因子结合位点，可能影响基因调控。当前分析为设计实验以解码耐药结核病的机制基础提供了宝贵见解。
